name: fresnel-flash-group
title: Fresnel Flash Group
description: A full-bleed hero/section background modelled on a rotating first-order Fresnel lens drum: eight glass panels ring a fixed lamp and turn at a steady 8-second lap, each panel's own glint sweeping past a fixed marker once a second, while the brighter primary panel's pass produces the station's identifying group flash once per lap.
useWhen: a full-bleed hero or section background that needs to read as continuously, mechanically alive rather than a looping blink or a static glow — the identity is a drum that never stops turning, with the identifying flash as a periodic consequence of that rotation rather than the whole spectacle. Pick arc-ladder-climb instead when the mechanism should be a discrete strike-climb-extinguish-restrike cycle on diverging rails rather than continuous rotation, or status-glyph-cadence when the surface is a small inline status glyph rather than a full-bleed background.
instruction: Build <FresnelFlashGroup children? className?> as a full-bleed Canvas 2D hero/section background modelling a rotating first-order Fresnel lens drum. GEOMETRY: computeGeo(W, H) derives drumRadius = minDim * 0.42, facetRadius = minDim * 0.052, lampRadius = minDim * 0.02, all centered at (W/2, H/2), plus a scale factor clamp(minDim / 640, 0.6, 1.6) applied to stroke widths and halo blur so the same numbers read from a card up to a 100vw hero. ROTATION: rotationAngleAt(elapsedMs) = (elapsedMs * 360/8000) % 360 is a pure function of elapsed time (never per-frame incremented state) — one full lap every 8.0s, which is also the station's published characteristic (Fl 8s). FACETS: 8 facets are placed at baseAngle = i * 45deg around the drum (0deg = 12 o'clock/up, clockwise), each facet's current angle = (baseAngle + rotation) % 360. A fixed camera-bearing marker sits at 0deg (12 o'clock); every facet's glint intensity is gaussian(angleDiff(facetAngle, 0), sigmaDeg) where angleDiff wraps to [-180,180] — non-primary facets use sigma=10deg and peak alpha 0.5 (so a glint crosses the marker every 1.0s, 8.0s/8 facets), while facet index 0 (the primary bullseye) uses a tighter sigma=6deg, peak alpha 1.0, a 1.2x wider dot, and a canvas shadowBlur halo (10px * scale * intensity) in --foreground — this is the station's identifying flash, firing once per 8.0s lap. Each facet's resting (non-glinting) alpha is 0.14 (0.22 for the primary) so the ring reads as structured even when nothing is aligned to the marker. BEAM LOBE: while the primary facet's intensity exceeds 0.01, a soft quadrilateral lobe is filled from two points just above the drum edge widening to the top of the canvas, using a vertical linear gradient from --foreground to --ns-muted, at globalAlpha = primaryIntensity * 0.5 — this ramps in and out over roughly a second on either side of the flash peak (never a single-frame blink) because it is driven directly by the same gaussian intensity value as the facet dot. HAZE: an independent slow drift keeps the dark interval between flashes visibly alive — a radial gradient (--foreground center to --ns-muted edge) at a constant 0.06 alpha, its center offset by sin/cos of a 21-second period at 0.16 * minDim amplitude, drawn every frame before the drum. LAMP: a small fixed dot at the exact center, --foreground at 0.55 alpha, constant, unrelated to rotation — represents the fixed lamp the drum rotates around. Colour is read once via getComputedStyle(document.documentElement) for --foreground and --ns-muted with zero literal fallback; if either is empty the mount loop retries on the next rAF and paints nothing until both resolve. A MutationObserver on document.documentElement's class attribute re-reads tokens on every theme flip; a ResizeObserver on the root recomputes geometry and resizes the canvas backing store (devicePixelRatio capped at 2) without resetting the elapsed-time clock; an IntersectionObserver stops driving new frames while off-screen and, on returning to view, re-reads tokens (picking up any theme flip that happened while hidden) and resumes the same continuous clock — no paint happens on any of these paths before a token read succeeds. Under prefers-reduced-motion the component runs zero rAF loops, zero timers: it calls the exact same drawScene(elapsedMs) function used by the live loop with elapsedMs pinned to STATIC_TIME_MS = 3400 (153deg into the 8.0s lap) — three facets partially lit at different values, none fully saturated (as the primary flash peak would be) and none in a fully-dark gap, the single most structured frame in the cycle — and never redraws. Cleanup on unmount cancels both the animation and token-wait rAF handles and disconnects all three observers. Optional children render over the field in a centered max-w-5xl column (eyebrow, headline, CTA), with pointer-events left to the canvas's aria-hidden sibling so nothing intercepts clicks meant for real content — there is no pointer tracking or hover state anywhere in this component, the rotation-and-flash cadence is the entire spectacle. Zero dependencies, DOM+canvas only, no colour literal anywhere including fallbacks.
